title: Plug a ribbon cable into a sensor board held up off its foam
instruction: Plug the ribbon cable into the box header on the green sensor board without pressing the parts under the board onto the mat.
context: Plugging keyed ribbon cables onto box headers is a common step in wiring sensors and robot electronics. A bare board with parts on its underside is held up by its edge while the cable is pressed in, so nothing under it is crushed.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. A white PLA riser block, 4.5 x 11 cm and 4 cm tall, at x 0.291 to 0.336 m, y -0.115 to -0.005 m, with a 3 mm dark grey anti-static rubber mat on top. On the mat, two grey polyurethane foam bars, 18 mm tall, 12 mm wide and 39 mm long (along x, x 0.293 to 0.332), centred at y -0.094 and -0.044. Across them lies a green FR4 sensor board, 50 x 80 x 1.6 mm (x 0.275 to 0.325, y -0.100 to -0.020), component side up, its near edge overhanging the riser by 16 mm; an orange PLA stiffener, 50 x 14 x 3 mm, is screwed under its left end (y -0.034 to -0.020). On the board: a black nylon shrouded 2 x 5 box header, 11.6 x 19.6 x 7 mm, centred at (0.30, -0.08), long along y, with a 5 mm key slot in the middle of its wall facing the robots; a black 8 mm chip. Under the board: the header's ten tin-plated pin tails, 2.4 mm long, and an electrolytic capacitor with a blue sleeve, 8 mm across and 15 mm tall, at (0.312, -0.069), its can 3 mm above the mat. Grey aluminium tray, 60 x 60 x 4 mm, at (0.22, -0.20); on it, the ribbon cable's black nylon IDC socket connector, 16 x 8 x 11 mm, its length along y and its 3.5 mm key towards the robots, with a 12 mm stub of grey ribbon cable, red stripe on one edge. Board 28 g, connector 4 g. Fixed layout matching the screenshot.
scoring: Measured at the end, relative to the board. 0 if the capacitor's can was ever within 0.5 mm of the mat during the trial (pressed onto it, which bends its leads), or the board ends tilted more than 30 degrees from component side up. Otherwise 0 unless the connector is in the header: its underside's centre within 1.5 mm of the header's centre, tilted no more than 10 degrees, and its underside no more than 6 mm above the board's top. 0.25 if it is in the header but not seated, or seated but a hand is still within 3 cm of it. 1.0 if it is seated (underside within 0.5 mm of its seat, 1.5 mm above the board) with its key in the header's slot and both hands clear of it.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull the connector out, stand it on the tray key towards the robots, and lay the board back across the foam bars as in the screenshot. In simulation the press fit is restored at each reset.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. Pins are not contacts: the connector rests on a sprung plate that gives at 1.2 N and lets it sink 2.5 mm to its seat (a real IDC fit takes more). Each foam bar is a rigid bar on a soft spring, 150 N/m. Bent capacitor leads are scored from the can's height above the mat, not modelled. The ribbon is a short rigid stub.
